html:
Tourism in the Maldives began in 1972, when the first resort, Kurumba, opened on an island near Male with a few dozen beds for visitors from Italy.

Before then the islands lived from fishing, coconuts and a little trade. The model that followed was one island, one resort: whole uninhabited islands were leased to hotel firms, keeping foreign visitors and their alcohol apart from the Muslim villages.

Within a few decades there were well over a hundred resorts, and tourism became the main source of money and jobs. It made the country one of the richest per head in South Asia, but left it exposed to shocks such as the tsunami of 2004 and to rising seas. The Sinamale Bridge of 2018 links Male to the airport island.
